profile.headline: Software Engineer at IBM Watson
profile.summary:
I am a recent graduate with a Master's degree in Physics and am seeking a career in computation. Studying physics has given me a strong foundation in problem solving and mathematics that is applicable to any technical field. Combine this with my dedicated self-study of programming and a passion for technology, and you get a strong candidate to join your team.

Much of my "real world" programming is in the field of medical imaging. As an undergraduate, I was employed in an imaging physics laboratory at UCI studying x-ray computed tomography and mammography. In particular, I implemented clustering algorithms to automatically segment images. MATLAB was the platform of choice, and I used it extensively during my research. One of my favorite projects was developing code to compute the Radon transform of an imaging phantom for CT simulations. 

I honestly love learning and am always exploring new topics and ideas. My current interests include: ITK, VTK, object oriented design, data science, and machine learning. Familiarity with the languages listed in my skills section ranges from exposure to advanced. I don't claim to be an expert in them, but I would love to have the opportunity to become one. If you can offer me a launch point for my career, I can offer you a quick-learning practiced problem solver with a solid foundation and enormous potential for growth.

To see some samples of my work, dereference this pointer: https://github.com/tjohnson31415.
There isn't much on there yet, so, if you need more convincing, I would happily complete a small programming assignment to showcase my abilities.

Thank you for your time and consideration!

positions.title: Associate Specialist
positions.description: Specialist in a medical physics research lab brought in to develop software algorithms to extract useful quantitative information from medical images. Frequently used my skills to quickly prototype and develop new algorithms and methods. Specific focuses include vessel extraction and morphology calculations in coronary CT angiography.

positions.title: Cable Installation Technician
positions.description: Seasonal employment for a small family owned specialty contractor installing structured cabling plants, i.e. data, voice, and coaxial cables. Worked during summers and breaks to help pay for school throughout my undergraduate years. Completed large projects to high quality standards. Repeat hire because of reliability, hard work, and attention to detail.

positions.title: Teaching Assistant
positions.description: Taught introductory physics to undergraduates for 20 hours per week. Two quarters as a lecture assistant: explained homework solutions and answered student questions, discussed and validated homework and exam questions with instructor. Five quarters as a lab instructor for weekly classes of 20+ students: responsible for ensuring that lab equipment functioned properly and grading all assignments with instructive feedback. Received positive reviews from instructors and students for all assignments. In TA evaluations, 84% of students would recommend to a friend.

positions.title: Research Assistant
positions.description: Performed research in an imaging physics laboratory. Studied computed tomography, mammography, MRI, and image processing. Involved in the complete imaging process from acquisition to analysis. Developed efficient implementations of clustering algorithms in MATLAB. Automated various computational tasks with scripts. Published two papers in peer-reviewed journals on the topic of breast density quantification and breast cancer risk.

publications.title: Breast density quantification using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) with bias field correction: A postmortem study
Breast density quantification with cone-beam CT: a post-mortem study
publications.publisher: Physics in Medicine and Biology · Jan 1, 2013
